## The sealed survey vault

Reach the pledged relic and free the surviving survey crew from its old defences.

People and truth. Corren knew repayment was overdue before telling Tavin it was settled. Eda legally acquired the pledge in good faith and spent money on a survey, but the plate is Lodge property Corren could not sell. Ysra wants the relic and an accurate record; her loyalty is not bought with a successful duel. At Eda’s camp, apprentice Myr is trapped behind the vault’s maintenance gate and foreman Kellin has escaped with a diagram. Eda offers to reduce her claim if Tavin rescues Myr and retrieves the crew’s instruments alongside the plate.

Compact vault. A camp approach enters B survey antechamber. From B, a guarded direct stair descends to D plate dais; a narrow maintenance passage reaches C counterweight room, then D from behind its pillar. E instrument store is barred from D and holds Myr. There is no world-altering Door here: the device projects local survey alignments and the plate supplies calibration marks. The scratched camp diagram identifies C, so a failed check never conceals the alternate route.

Antechamber defence. A damaged Warden Armor guards the direct stair. Its floor pattern includes a maintenance stripe; Intelligence (Investigation or Arcana) DC 12 interprets the worn symbol and permits a slow safe passage along that stripe. Failure leaves the symbol unclear, not the armour already attacking. Kellin’s diagram or spending time tracing the stripe from C supplies another way. Crossing the guarded stair without resolving its command starts the prepared fight. Spells act according to actual target restrictions; an enchantment valid against a humanoid does not necessarily affect a construct.

Counterweight hazard. A visibly frayed chain supports C’s narrow walkway. A secured rope or a braced ladder bypasses the risk. Rushing unsupported requires Dexterity save DC 11; failure causes 1d4 bludgeoning on a shallow fall and leaves the character below the walkway with a ladder route back. Tools DC 11 locks the counterweight before crossing; a failed attempt costs a pin or time if that was stated, and warns that the chain is moving. Do not create a second surprise damage trap behind the same check.

Plate and prisoner. The plate rests on a pressure cradle. Myr can call out its paired hand-release from E. Releasing Myr uses the key at C, thieves’ tools DC 12 or lifting a bent bar with Strength DC 12; failure alerts the guardian if still active but does not collapse the vault. Two people holding the releases, or an equivalent supported tool arrangement, remove the plate safely. Removing it blindly closes D’s gate; its manual catch remains accessible with tools DC 12 from either side. The store contains the crew’s 20 gp of instruments.

Free Myr before touching the plate, or accept the extra access problem caused by acting without their warning.

Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.

The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.

Baseline: one level-1 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns. Tavin Bell’s accepted Character File owns their actual equipment and class resources.

Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. ## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

### Encounter adjudication

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## GM guidance

Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.

Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.

Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.

Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

## Completion and aftermath

The predator has left or been stopped, or the party and surviving Nessa and Orlo have escaped by the ditch to safe ground. Account for either person lost through actual play; an intention to retreat is not an escape.

The medicine and flour are each recorded as carried out, left at the wagon, consumed or lost through play. Record the wagon and any keepsake actually recovered; rescuing property is not required after the people are safe.

Closing event: on safe ground Nessa responds to the actual rescue and losses and settles the agreed assistance payment if able. If she was lost, Orlo or the receiving Guild contact takes the report instead. No additional delivery adventure is required.

## Failure and withdrawal

Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.

Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

# Pip Venn

Human Rogue, level 2. Pronouns: they/them.

Quick with a grin; checks that everyone has an exit. No fixed home, allegiance, or campaign history is assigned.

## Playing Pip

Use a shortsword or shortbow and seek a Sneak Attack opening. You have two Expertise choices; Cunning Action arrives at level two. Expertise: Stealth and Perception. Thieves' Cant is known.

## Creation choices

Standard array, then the Criminal background increases, is reflected in the final ability scores. Criminal supplies its listed skills, tool, and origin feat. Human Versatile supplies Skilled; Skillful supplies history. Skilled choices: insight survival deception. Class skill choices: acrobatics investigation perception persuasion. Starting equipment uses class option A and background option A, with 24 GP retained. Languages: Common, Dwarvish, and Elvish. Human Resourceful grants Heroic Inspiration after a Long Rest.

All identity, personality, background, ability, equipment, skill, and spell choices can be changed on an independent copy. Keep the declared creation rules when changing mechanical choices.

## Prepared level-two choices

Dash, Disengage or Hide as a Bonus Action. Fixed HP increase, including Constitution: 7.

# The Cartographer’s Wake

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A stolen chart at a Nexus wake points to a sealed survey vault. Track the thieves, brave the old works and recover the mapmaker’s last expedition record.

Tone: A brisk investigation leading into a dangerous Warden ruin.

A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

## The last route

Trace the stolen chart into the survey annex and resolve custody of the recovered field record.

Cast and truth. Ula wants Seren’s bequest honoured. Former assistant Pera copied the chart to protect a refuge named on it, but did not steal the original. A local buyer, Hadrik, hired two opportunists to take the original before the bequest could restrict its sale. Davren the scholar wants credit; refuge representative Nalin wants consultation. Hadrik’s crew is using the chart to reach Seren’s field case in a small abandoned Warden survey annex beneath the bookshop quarter. Neither map nor case contains the Rift Awakening’s Door secrets.

Investigation with useful outcomes. The broken cellar latch, muddy blue chalk and porter’s description all identify the annex route without a roll. An Intelligence (Investigation) DC 12 check matches a scrap to Pera’s harmless tracing, separating her activity from the theft; on failure Ula’s dated receipt supplies that distinction after a conversation. A Wisdom (Survival) DC 12 trail check locates a dry maintenance crawlway and avoids the guarded landing. Otherwise the clear main stair still reaches the annex. Persuasion DC 12 persuades the frightened porter to sketch the sentry’s position; failure leaves the position unknown, not the route blocked.

Site and connections. A: the cellar stair descends to B, a 20-foot-square landing, with a side crawlway to C. B’s guarded arch reaches C, a disused instrument hall, and a barred door to D, the keeper’s office. C and D both connect to E, the survey vault. All passages are ordinary navigable space; give a clear sketch or descriptions before the player chooses a route. The landing has waist-high crates offering half cover. The crawlway is cramped but carries no automatic damage or exhaustion.

Instrument hall trap. Copper tripwire crosses the clearly scuffed plinth. Searching the plinth reveals the wire; Investigation DC 12 identifies the counterweight and a wedge point. Disable with thieves’ tools and a Dexterity check DC 12, wedge it with a ten-foot pole from safety, or go through D. A failed disable attempt snaps the wire: Dexterity save DC 12, 1d6 bludgeoning on failure, no damage on success, then the trap is spent. The keeper’s door opens with the sentry’s key, tools DC 12, or Strength DC 14; forcing it warns the vault occupant. The office is defensible for a short rest if entrances are secured; a rest gives Hadrik’s surviving hireling time to negotiate or carry the loose chart toward the known exit, never vanish off-map.

Vault decision and loot. The original chart lies on a reading stand and the field case is locked beneath it. A repeated three-notch symbol on the map and stand identifies its release; careful examination suffices, or a tools check DC 12 opens it noisily. Taking the case without disengaging the guardian causes the prepared second encounter. The guardian has a physical shutoff behind the far pillar; reach it and use an action with the office key, or use tools DC 12 while exposed. Failure costs the action. No roll erases the guardian from initiative before the mechanism is actually used. The case contains route notes, Nalin’s consultation letter and 15 gp worth of legitimate survey fittings. Ula’s 25 gp fee is separate. Distribute the chart according to the actual bequest and choices, then close with the wake’s unfinished toast.

## GM guidance

Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.

The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.

Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.

Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

## Completion and aftermath

The survey-annex recovery has ended with the party outside it and the original chart and field case each recovered into named custody or reported lost or left at a known position. Establish Hadrik's theft separately from Pera's protective copy through the prepared evidence.

Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

## Optional continuation

Further adventures require the player’s interest after this story has a complete ending. Surviving contacts and obligations can carry forward.
