Place the combat when its stated event occurs; establish the immediate surroundings naturally. Resolve combat, checks, spells and recovery through the Ruleset. Negotiation, stealth, retreat and supported abilities can change an encounter's outcome; do not replace a bypassed fight with another mandatory fight.
planned_encounters: 5A — Hospital and streets, level 10: displaced predators or Rift manifestations (retained Air/Fire/Earth Elemental profiles, using their real damage types) and rogue Animated Armor. Protect evacuating people and access to the workshop; success preserves those neighborhoods in the aftermath.

5B — Bypass workshop, level 10: Halvek's or the culpable Edda's defenders (Gladiator/Bandit Captain/Scout), with a Shield Guardian if the party warrants it. Do not add the guardian if its presence overwhelms a small party. Operators surrender when their promises are disproved or defense collapses.

5C — Root Gate approach, level 11: Warden custodians (Shield Guardian with its actual control amulet held by a named custodian, or a Stone Golem for a larger party). Recovered maintenance authority, careful infiltration or a fight can secure access. This approach remains cleared afterward.
situations: Arrival in Nexus. Palla offers the Anchor's Rest as a base, with visiting scholars, neighbors and food from many remembered homes. Visit the Crossroads, Riftborn Quarter, Athenaeum and Undercroft entrances at the player's pace. Invite Companions to take an interest in a person, job or cause of their own; do not write an unchosen romance or tell the PC they now love the city. People from earlier acts can arrive with refugees, trade or research if the party's actions gave them reason. Let ordinary side stories and quiet days establish what a decision to stay might contain.

The city's disagreement. Physician Asha Ren protects the Athenaeum hospital and treats the injured regardless of faction. SL-born council delegate Miren Holt wants containment, informed consent and a guarantee that no experiment expends her constituents. Returner delegates want access to early return rather than another indefinite shutdown. Edda can represent them if she retained trust; otherwise a named survivor or local organizer speaks without inheriting her culpability. V can provide expertise without automatically chairing the meeting. Palla wants facts clear enough that ordinary people can make choices. None needs to be convinced that wanting home is shameful.

The civic surge. A section of the Riftborn Quarter begins phasing while hospital equipment and nearby Anchor markers pulse together. Give visible warning and a chance to help before casualties, not a surprise city-wide death toll during a tavern conversation. The cause is a new illegal mass-passage bypass connected from a Returner workshop into the Undercroft civic regulator. Edda authorized it only if she knowingly persisted after the earlier evidence; otherwise Dain's surviving cell or the already-established engineer Halvek continued it against her wishes. Introduce Halvek in the workshop's public commissioning records before the confrontation, not as an endless replacement villain.

Rescue and investigation. The hospital and occupied blocks need an evacuation route while the party finds and isolates the connection. Displaced beasts and awakened constructs make that dangerous. Asha can manage patients if protected, and district crews can do ordinary evacuation work; the PC need not personally carry everyone. Live wiring and stamped installation orders establish the cause. The workshop ledger holds copies if machinery is destroyed. Confront the responsible operators, expose what they knew and end the bypass. A failed isolation can still lead to a completed evacuation, with damaged wards and homes honestly recorded. The city pays 300 gp for the resolved operation or evacuation, and makes ordinary supplies available for the final expedition.

The Awakening. After the civic crisis the party can compare the accumulated timings: Thornwall roots, Glasshouse, the Cairnfields and now Nexus. Distant tears connect into a violet horizon. A common pulse is audible across districts, and shadows briefly fall toward the same absent light. The wound is beginning to act as one. It is neither a voice nor a new deity. Use an announced change in physical conditions to create urgency; do not silently advance a hidden clock for every side conversation. The coalition can evacuate vulnerable areas and plan the final work, but indefinite delay after this warning carries visibly worsening consequences.

The Root Gate approach. Athenaeum service stairs and an established Undercroft smuggling route both lead toward the regulator. Asha can secure official access; a local crew can sell or give the alternate directions in recognition of the civic rescue. The approach is occupied by Warden constructs and any radical holdouts actually left in play. Clear, bypass or negotiate through them and compare the atlas/manual with the controls. This produces a concrete operation: preserve containment and restore elective individual return, or preserve containment with elective return shut. A forced mass bypass is physically available but its recorded and visible consequences are explained before it is chosen.

Commitment. Miren convenes the coalition at the Athenaeum, or district representatives meet at Palla's if formal leaders refuse. Assign who operates controls, who handles evacuation and who maintains the protected approach. The party can choose capable volunteers, themselves or actual allies; no unique class, ancestry, optional favor or perfect faction approval is necessary. Record opposition and promises without pretending unanimity. Securing the approach and committing an executable operation grants the final milestone; give the party the Ruleset's actual level-up choices before Act 6. The city lends each participant one suitable ordinary weapon, armor suit or tool needed for the operation from its actual armory, with return or loss accounted for after the finale; heavy armor still requires the character's normal training and rules.
structure.summary: Levels 10–12. Live in Nexus long enough to value it, stop a civic disaster, and bring a coalition to the regulator beneath the city.
structure.title: Act 5 — A City Worth Leaving

branches: A legitimate override can avoid the Engine battle without losing the climax: performing the chosen operation and personal decisions remain substantive play.
Successful containment can coexist with an imperfect coalition, V never being forgiven or a Companion choosing to leave.
If the party chooses an unsafe operation or fails, resolve the actual losses and escape. An early withdrawal is an honest failed campaign ending, not completion of unplayed successful milestones.
consequences: Maintain the world after any personal departure. People, property, children, promises, injuries and political decisions are not erased when the outside trip ends.
No new mandatory act begins after the Nexus aftermath. Optional local play uses the surviving world and the same level-12 cap unless the user explicitly commissions a revised Plan.
dynamic_encounter_guidance: Use the opposition guide in this Plan's contained Setting for the named retained SRD profiles and party-size guidance. Place the combat when its stated event occurs; establish the immediate surroundings naturally. Resolve combat, checks, spells and recovery through the Ruleset. Negotiation, stealth, retreat and supported abilities can change an encounter's outcome; do not replace a bypassed fight with another mandatory fight.
planned_encounters: 6A — Root Gate regulator, level 12: Vigilant Engine (SRD Stone Golem). For PC plus one Companion consider the declared damaged-custodian variant in the opposition guide; for a robust larger party add only warranted Animated Armor or a separate earlier custodian encounter. The Engine attacks those forcing the controls, obeys an authenticated override and stops when defeated. Objective: gain usable control or withdraw with an honest failure result.

6B — Interrupted final operation: only holdouts or manifestations established by the actual chosen operation may interfere (Gladiator/elemental profiles already used). A cooperative Edda is not forced into a betrayal, and a contained wound does not spawn a final surprise boss. Combat supports the performed operation, not an arbitrary kill total.
situations: Before the descent. At the Anchor's Rest or the defended Athenaeum staging area, give the party one genuine chance to speak with each other and chosen friends. Volunteers reaffirm their consent and the coalition checks the actual operation. These are conversations, not loyalty checks required to unlock survival. The Root Gate approach stays in the state established in Act 5; do not repopulate it to consume fresh resources. Let the Ruleset determine rests and available resources. No additional travel or crafting subsystem is introduced.

The Vigilant Engine. The final regulator houses the last active custodian of Closed Vigil. Its role is to prevent a repeat of the mass-passage catastrophe, and its obsolete orders treat restoration of elective return as sabotage. It demands maintenance authorization, identifies the forbidden bypass and offers indefinite shutdown as its only approved solution. It is a construct with a recorded directive, not secretly V or a god. Present its instruction clearly enough to debate, deceive with evidence, lawfully supersede or oppose. The observatory manual and atlas together contain the legitimate procedure for ending Closed Vigil; the Engine can be persuaded through demonstrated compliance with that procedure, not a generic ungrounded charm roll.

The confrontation. Default to a serious fight against the Engine if the party insists on operating beyond its orders without satisfying the authenticated override. Its body uses the Stone Golem profile, with support only as appropriate to the actual party. Defeating its body allows access; no secret invulnerability phase or optional item is required. An earned override disarms it and leaves a potentially valuable custodian. If the party loses, retreat through the secured approach and evacuate the threatened districts if still possible. An intact Engine continues its failing shutdown; do not narrate a safe restoration the party did not perform.

Performing the operation. The actual work has three named tasks: disconnect the mass-passage bypass, set the regulator to distribute containment across the surviving anchors, then choose the individual-return interlock's open or closed setting. The atlas identifies circuits, the manual identifies controls, and the Root Gate labels confirm them. Skilled work, admitted magic, allied operators or direct manual operation can complete these tasks; no single roll decides the fate of the world. Uncertain checks resolve particular attempts and consequences explained beforehand. If interruption damages the controls, the manual provides a containment-only fallback using the accessible emergency isolator. That fallback can save the region but leave elective return unavailable pending later repairs.

What each result means. Regulated return plus containment quiets the linked tears without destroying ordinary crossings. The Door admits willing Riftborn individually after a witnessed consent and identity check; locals cannot be transferred because there is no outside body to receive them. Containment-only also saves the region but leaves early-return advocates with a real grievance and an unresolved future project. Forcing the mass bypass replicates the known failure: neighboring anchors overload, districts phase and casualties follow actual exposure and evacuation. Stop it in time and a damaged containment fallback may still hold. If the region is lost, native lives end locally and permanently dead Riftborn return; do not call that everybody getting a happy trip home.

Stay or leave. Explain the established memory loss before the PC chooses. A safe Door remains available under its actual agreed custody; staying today need not mean an invented irreversible vow never to leave. Each Companion decides independently, using the relationship and priorities developed in play. The PC may stay while a Companion leaves, leave while others stay, or arrange another feasible future. The party cannot take SL-born children into a nonexistent outside life or force an unwilling person through. A PC returning now experiences a brief ordinary outside awakening, with no clear encyclopedic memories, transferable powers or convenient wealth. The Severed Lands and the people left there continue.

The immediate ending. At the surviving Nexus gathering, give the actual result to Asha, Miren, Palla and surviving delegates or their named successors. Record who holds the regulator, what oversight and access were agreed, V's confession/accountability or unresolved absence, Edda's return/stay/detention/death, and the neighborhoods and people lost. Resolve the prepared party farewells or welcome before offering continued local adventure to a staying PC or Finish the story. If the PC has already departed, use a brief external closing glimpse of those left behind rather than claiming the PC knows it. Optional after-story follows only if the player finishes: it grows from actual relationships and choices, not a preset marriage, children or mandatory death scene.

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. # Last Cart Through

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

### Encounter adjudication

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## GM guidance

Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.

Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.

Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.

Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

## Completion and aftermath

The predator has left or been stopped, or the party and surviving Nessa and Orlo have escaped by the ditch to safe ground. Account for either person lost through actual play; an intention to retreat is not an escape.

The medicine and flour are each recorded as carried out, left at the wagon, consumed or lost through play. Record the wagon and any keepsake actually recovered; rescuing property is not required after the people are safe.

Closing event: on safe ground Nessa responds to the actual rescue and losses and settles the agreed assistance payment if able. If she was lost, Orlo or the receiving Guild contact takes the report instead. No additional delivery adventure is required.

## Failure and withdrawal

Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.

Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

## Optional continuation

Only after resolving this adventure, ask whether the player wants to pursue a surviving relationship or optional lead. The ending does not depend on accepting.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

# Bram Alder

Human Fighter, level 2. Pronouns: they/them.

Steady and dry-witted; likes a clear plan and a hot meal. No fixed home, allegiance, or campaign history is assigned.

## Playing Bram

A direct greatsword fighter in chain mail. Attack on your turn and use Second Wind when hurt; you begin with two uses.

## Creation choices

Standard array, then the Soldier background increases, is reflected in the final ability scores. Soldier supplies its listed skills, tool, and origin feat. Human Versatile supplies Skilled; Skillful supplies nature. Skilled choices: survival acrobatics stealth. Class skill choices: perception insight. Starting equipment uses class option A and background option A, with 18 GP retained. Languages: Common, Dwarvish, and Elvish. Human Resourceful grants Heroic Inspiration after a Long Rest.

All identity, personality, background, ability, equipment, skill, and spell choices can be changed on an independent copy. Keep the declared creation rules when changing mechanical choices.

## Prepared level-two choices

Action Surge, one use per Short or Long Rest. Tactical Mind uses Second Wind; retain Defense. Fixed HP increase, including Constitution: 8.
